2026-05-18.edu_title: What Credit Ratings Actually Mean for Your Money
edu_points: Credit ratings (AAA→D) grade how likely a borrower is to repay its debt.
A downgrade raises borrowing costs — the U.S. could pay billions more in interest.
Moody's, S&P, and Fitch are the 'Big 3' agencies that rate countries and companies.
Lower ratings signal higher risk, pushing investors to demand better returns.
Even one notch down can trigger sell-offs in bonds, stocks, and the currency.

2026-05-20.edu_title: Dollar-Cost Averaging: Invest Smarter, Not Harder
edu_points: Invest a fixed amount on a schedule — weekly or monthly — no matter the price
You automatically buy more shares when prices dip and fewer when they rise
It eliminates emotional trading and the trap of trying to time the market
Even $50 per month compounded over 30 years can grow to six figures
DCA works best with broad index funds and ETFs — low cost, diversified

2026-05-21.edu_title: How to Read Earnings Reports Like a Pro
edu_points: EPS beat = stock usually jumps; a miss means analysts expected more profit than delivered
Revenue growth shows if the company is winning more customers and expanding market share
Guidance (future outlook) moves stock prices more than any single past quarter result
Operating margin reveals how much profit remains after covering all core business costs
Always compare year-over-year (YoY) — quarterly seasonality can distort the real picture

2026-05-23.edu_title: What Is an ETF? The Easiest Way to Own the Market
edu_points: An ETF (Exchange-Traded Fund) holds a basket of stocks you can buy like a single share.
One S&P 500 ETF gives you instant exposure to 500 top U.S. companies at once.
ETFs have ultra-low fees — often under 0.1% per year vs. 1%+ for mutual funds.
They trade on exchanges all day, giving you flexibility that mutual funds don't offer.
Beginners love ETFs: low cost, instant diversification, and no stock-picking needed.

edu_points: Agents break big goals into smaller tasks, then act step-by-step autonomously
They use 'tools' — web search, code execution, APIs — to interact with the world
A feedback loop lets them check their own output and self-correct mistakes

2026-05-28.edu_title: Moore's Law: Why Chips Keep Getting Faster
edu_points: Moore's Law predicts transistor count doubles ~every 2 years, boosting speed & efficiency.
Today's 2nm chips pack 100 billion+ transistors into a space smaller than a fingernail.
More transistors = faster processing, less power draw, and smarter AI at lower cost.
Smaller nodes are harder to make — only TSMC & Samsung lead at the 2nm level today.
As physics limits shrink, chipmakers turn to 3D stacking and new materials to keep pace.

2026-05-30.edu_title: The Rule of 72: How to Double Your Money
edu_points: Divide 72 by your annual return rate to find years to double your money.
At 6% return: 72 ÷ 6 = 12 years to double — no calculator needed.
Higher returns compound faster: 10% return doubles money in ~7.2 years.
Works for debt too — 18% APR credit card doubles what you owe in 4 years.
Einstein reportedly called compound interest the '8th wonder of the world'.
